1.title: Report Settings: Export, Mobile, Personalization, Accessibility and Refresh
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Report Settings: Export, Mobile, Personalization, Accessibility and Refresh. It covers the exam area Visualize and analyze the data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Configure export settings. Design reports for mobile devices. Enable personalization in a report, including personalized visuals. Design and configure Power B I reports for accessibility. Configure automatic page refresh. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Visualize and analyze the data (twenty-five-thirty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Export settings
1.text: Export settings. Report-level export settings decide what viewers can take out of a report. In Desktop, go to File, Options, Current file, Report settings, then the Export data group.

1.title: Export settings, continued
1.text: Export settings. The figure shows this: Map of the report settings in this module: export, mobile layout, personalization, accessibility and automatic page refresh.

1.title: Export settings, continued
1.text: Export settings. Summarized data. The data shown in the visual. Summarized and underlying data. Also the rows behind the visual. No export. Nothing at all. Rules that exams test. Admin portal settings override the report setting. If the admin restricts export, the report setting cannot loosen it. Exporting underlying data needs Build permission on the semantic model. Row-level security limits the exported rows to what the viewer may see. Excel formats keep the sensitivity label; C S V does not.

1.title: Export settings, continued
1.text: Export settings. Excel from a live connection (service). five hundred thousand rows. Excel (.xlsx). one hundred fifty thousand rows. C S V, service or Desktop. thirty thousand rows. Exam tip: Three report options: summarized only, summarized and underlying, or none. The admin portal wins over the report setting, and underlying data needs Build permission. Exam tip: Row limits: C S V thirty thousand; Excel one hundred fifty thousand; Excel from a live connection five hundred thousand. Row-level security can shrink the export further.

1.title: Mobile layout
1.text: Mobile layout. A mobile layout is a portrait phone design for a report page. It is made in Desktop and shown only in the Power B I mobile apps. Where. Mobile layout on the View tab. Canvas. A portrait phone canvas on a grid. Visuals. The Page visuals pane lists the page's visuals; drag them onto the canvas. Auto-create. Builds a first layout that you then adjust. Where it shows. Only in the Power B I mobile apps, on i O S and Android. Publishing. Publishing the report publishes the mobile layout too.

1.title: Mobile layout, continued
1.text: Mobile layout. Design each page on its own: put the key visual first and keep few visuals on the phone canvas. Exam tip: The mobile layout appears only in the Power B I mobile apps. It is created per page in Desktop on the View tab, and publishing the report publishes it.

1.title: Personalization
1.text: Personalization. Personalized visuals let viewers change a visual without editing the report. The author turns the setting on. Setting. Report settings, Personalize visuals: in Desktop under File, Options, Current file; in the service in the report Settings. Viewers can. Change the visual type, swap a measure or dimension, add or remove a legend, compare measures, change the aggregation. Where. In Reading view. Saving. As a personal bookmark; reset returns to the author's default. Author control. Turn it off for a page or a single visual. Perspectives. Can limit the fields viewers see, but a perspective is not security.

1.title: Personalization, continued
1.text: Personalization. To restrict data, use row-level security or object-level security, never a perspective. Exam tip: Personalize visuals is a report setting that lets viewers change the visual type, measure, legend and aggregation, and save the result as a personal bookmark. Perspectives limit fields but are not security.

1.title: Accessibility
1.text: Accessibility. Some accessibility features are built in. Others you configure. Keyboard navigation. Alt text. Screen-reader support. Tab order. High contrast colors. Titles and labels. Focus mode. Markers. Show data table (Alt plus Shift plus F eleven). Themes and contrast.

1.title: Accessibility, continued
1.text: Accessibility. Alt text. Format visual, General, Alt text; up to two hundred fifty characters; describe what the visual shows. Tab order. Selection pane, Tab order; remove decorative items. Titles and labels. Give every visual and page a clear title. Markers. Turn on Show Markers and use different shapes for each series. Contrast. Text and background at least four point five to one (W C A G two point one). Themes. Use an accessible theme, color-blind friendly or high contrast. Do not use color alone to carry meaning. Report tooltips are not read by screen readers. Exam tip: Alt text holds up to two hundred fifty characters, and contrast must be at least four point five to one. Remove decorative items from the tab order and use markers so that series differ by more than color.

1.title: Automatic page refresh
1.text: Automatic page refresh. Automatic page refresh updates the visuals on a page at a set time or when data changes. It works for Direct Query, not Import. It is not the scheduled refresh of an Import model (Module fourteen).

1.title: Automatic page refresh, continued
1.text: Automatic page refresh. Supported sources. Direct Query; a composite model follows its most restrictive source; some live connections. Not supported. Import models. Page refresh card. Shown in the Format pane for reports that use Direct Query. Types. Fixed interval or change detection; each page uses one. Fixed interval default. thirty minutes in Desktop. Fixed interval minimum. one second in Desktop; thirty minutes on shared capacity; five minutes by default on Premium or Fabric.

1.title: Automatic page refresh, continued
1.text: Automatic page refresh. Change detection. Polls one measure per model; refreshes only when its value changes. Change detection availability. Premium or Fabric capacity workspaces only, never shared capacity. Change detection minimum. five seconds by default.

1.title: Automatic page refresh, continued
1.text: Automatic page refresh. The capacity admin sets the minimum intervals and can turn the feature off. Exam tip: Import is not supported; change detection needs a Premium or Fabric capacity workspace. Fixed interval on shared capacity cannot go below thirty minutes. Exam tip: Change detection polls one measure per model and refreshes the page only when that value changes. Fixed interval refreshes on every tick of the timer.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A report must let viewers export only what each visual shows and never the rows underneath. Which report setting should the author choose? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Export of summarized data only, no row detail. The summarized data option exports the visual's data only, while the underlying option also exposes the rows behind it.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An author turns on the report setting that allows export of summarized and underlying data, yet viewers cannot export anything from the service. What is the most likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: An admin portal tenant setting restricts export. Admin portal settings override the report-level export setting.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A report looks right on a desktop screen, and the author wants a portrait layout for phones. Where is it created, and where does it appear? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: In Mobile layout on the View tab; in Power B I mobile apps. The mobile layout is created from the View tab and is used only in the Power B I mobile apps.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An author wants viewers to turn a column chart into a line chart and save their own version, without editing the report. What should the author turn on? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Personalize visuals in the report settings. Personalize visuals lets viewers change the visual type and save the result as a personal bookmark.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A screen reader user cannot tell what a chart shows, and a keyboard user must tab through decorative images before reaching the charts. Which actions fix both problems? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Add chart alt text and remove images from the tab order. Alt text describes the chart to a screen reader, and removing decorative items from the tab order lets keyboard users skip them.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A Direct Query report in a workspace on shared capacity must refresh a page only when new orders arrive. Why can the author not use change detection? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Change detection needs a Premium or Fabric workspace. Change detection works only in workspaces on a Premium or Fabric capacity, not on shared capacity.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What are the three report-level export options? Answer: Summarized data, summarized and underlying data, or no export. Question two. What is the C S V export row limit? Answer: thirty thousand rows. Question three. Where does a mobile layout appear? Answer: Only in the Power B I mobile apps.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. How many characters can alt text hold? Answer: Up to two hundred fifty characters. Question five. What is the minimum contrast ratio for text? Answer: four point five to one. Question six. Which storage mode does automatic page refresh not support? Answer: Import.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Export options: Summarized data, summarized and underlying data, or none; admin portal overrides. Export limits: C S V thirty thousand rows; Excel one hundred fifty thousand; Excel from a live connection five hundred thousand. Mobile layout: View tab, Mobile layout; portrait grid; Page visuals pane; auto-create. Personalization: Personalize visuals report setting; change type, measure, legend, aggregation; personal bookmarks. Accessibility: Alt text two hundred fifty characters; tab order; markers; contrast four point five to one; accessible themes. Automatic page refresh: Direct Query, not Import; fixed interval or change detection. Refresh minimums: Fixed: one second Desktop, thirty minutes shared, five minutes default on capacity.
